17  Construct Clinic IDs

Carry reviewed clinic identities across GESIS changes

This page builds the clinic-month identity crosswalk from the legacy monthly inventory, the cleaned DHIS2–GESIS mapping, and the reviewed GESIS corrections. The reviewed rules below remain explicit so their effects can be checked before the resulting IDs are used downstream.

Important Prerequisite: Make The Legacy Monthly Inventory Available

This stage begins by reading in a set of raw data “from Kevin” that is used to define “unique clinic months”.

The cleaned mapping is the s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df target from the preceding page.

Tip Procedure: Declare Inputs And Identity Helpers

targets tracks the source archive and the rebuilt Parquet inventory as files, while the mapping dependency uses the preceding page’s in-memory data target. The selectors resolve reviewed inputs from the staged-input inventory rather than relying on the old script’s working directory.

library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(stringi)
library(duckplyr)

s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE) {
  if (na.rm) x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  values <- unique(x)
  values[which.max(tabulate(match(x, values)))]
}

s2_clinic_ids_first_fn <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) NA else dplyr::first(x)
}

s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn <- function(paths, pattern) {
  matches <- stringr::str_subset(paths, pattern)
  if (length(matches) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected one staged input matching /", pattern, "/; found ", length(matches), ".")
  }
  matches
}

The archived legacy script selects the six identity columns and removes duplicates within each monthly CSV before combining files. Keeping the health measurement columns would repeat every identity for each reported measurement. We perform that reduction in DuckDB and write one Parquet artifact per member.

Only YYYY_MM.csv members in mdg_tall_split/ are selected. This reproduces the legacy numeric-filename selection for this freeze and excludes missing_date.csv, diar_pneu_fix.csv, AVC.csv, and macOS metadata. Sorting the members reproduces the legacy list.files() order.

The 120 monthly CSVs in the May 2025 freeze use Windows-1252. A complete byte scan found 9C, A8, E0, E8, E9, EB, and F4 outside ASCII. For example, Ampitafà contains byte E0, and Sœurs contains 9C; the latter distinguishes Windows-1252 from ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1). A UTF-8 process locale does not change these file bytes, and Latin-1 is not a valid substitute for this archive.

Use DuckDB’s official encodings extension with encoding = "CP1252". INSTALL reuses the installed extension after the first download; a new runtime or DuckDB version needs network access for that download. LOAD runs on duckplyr’s own connection in each worker. Decoding happens in DuckDB before reduction, leaving UTF-8 names in Parquet without loading the tall CSV into R or skipping invalid rows. The staged archive stays unchanged.

s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn <- function() {
  c("cNom", "cAnnee", "cPeriode", "cCodeNiv", "cCodeStru", "fname")
}

s2_clinic_months_list_members_fn <- function(archive_path) {
  members <- utils::unzip(archive_path, list = TRUE)$Name
  members <- members[
    grepl("(^|/)mdg_tall_split/[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}\\.csv$", members) &
      !grepl("(^|/)__MACOSX/", members)
  ]
  stopifnot(length(members) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(basename(members)))
  sort(members, method = "radix")
}

s2_clinic_months_write_member_fn <- function(archive_path, member, output_path) {
  stopifnot(
    length(archive_path) == 1L, file.exists(archive_path),
    length(member) == 1L,
    !grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)", member)
  )

  extraction_dir <- tempfile("clinic-month-")
  dir.create(extraction_dir)
  on.exit(unlink(extraction_dir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  csv_path <- utils::unzip(archive_path, files = member, exdir = extraction_dir)
  stopifnot(length(csv_path) == 1L, file.exists(csv_path))

  # Read text first: read.csv() keeps empty clinic names but treats NA as missing.
  # Cast only the five numeric identity fields, matching the archived integers.
  column_types <- c(
    cNom = "VARCHAR", cAnnee = "VARCHAR", cPeriode = "VARCHAR",
    cCodeNiv = "VARCHAR", cCodeStru = "VARCHAR", cCode = "VARCHAR",
    fname = "VARCHAR", Variable = "VARCHAR", Value = "VARCHAR"
  )
  source_file <- basename(member)
  identity_columns <- s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn()
  integer_columns <- setdiff(identity_columns, "cNom")
  duckplyr::db_exec("INSTALL encodings")
  duckplyr::db_exec("LOAD encodings")
  result <- read_csv_duckdb(
    csv_path,
    prudence = "stingy",
    options = list(
      header = TRUE, delim = ",", quote = "\"", escape = "\"",
      types = list(column_types), nullstr = "NA", encoding = "CP1252"
    )
  ) |>
    select(all_of(identity_columns)) |>
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(integer_columns),
        ~ as.integer(if_else(.x == "", NA_character_, .x))
      ),
      .inventory_row = row_number()
    ) |>
    summarise(.inventory_row = min(.inventory_row), .by = all_of(identity_columns)) |>
    mutate(.inventory_file = source_file) |>
    arrange(.inventory_row)

  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}

s2_clinic_months_write_inventory_fn <- function(input_paths, output_path) {
  input_paths <- unname(as.character(input_paths))
  stopifnot(length(input_paths) > 0L, all(file.exists(input_paths)))

  # Read all branch artifacts as one relation; retain repeats across source files.
  result <- read_parquet_duckdb(input_paths, prudence = "stingy") |>
    arrange(.inventory_file, .inventory_row)
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}
#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_raw_zip <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "(^|/)madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning\\.zip$"
)
s2_clinic_months_members_chr <- s2_clinic_months_list_members_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip
)

The execution page declares a dynamic branch per archive member, producing s2_clinic_months_deduplicated_parquet. Each branch extracts into its own temporary directory and deletes the CSV after the Parquet write finishes. prudence = "stingy" prevents accidental fallback that would materialize raw data in R. Only artifact paths cross the targets boundary.

The combined inventory deliberately retains repeats across files, matching the legacy procedure. .inventory_file and .inventory_row record file order and the first source-row position for each identity. They preserve first-occurrence tie breaking in the downstream mode calculations; SQL grouping alone does not guarantee that order.

#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet <- s2_clinic_months_write_inventory_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_deduplicated_parquet,
  here::here("data", "intermediates", "unique_clinic_months_v1-2.parquet")
)

It looks like we need to load a file with GESIS corrections:

s2_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE\\.xlsx$"
)

s2_gesis_code_corrections_integer_df <- read_excel(s2_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`) & `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") %>% 
  setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) %>% 
  unique() %>%
  mutate(old_code = as.integer(old_code), correct_code = as.integer(correct_code))

And join it onto the gesis crosswalk mapping file:

#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_corrected_parquet <- {
  result <- s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet %>%
    read_parquet_duckdb() %>%
    left_join(
      s2_gesis_code_corrections_integer_df %>%
        select(cCodeStru = old_code, correct_cCodeStru = correct_code)
    ) %>% 
    mutate(
      correct_cCodeStru = if_else(is.na(correct_cCodeStru), cCodeStru, correct_cCodeStru)) 
 
  output_path <- here::here("data", "intermediates", "unique_clinic_months_corrected.parquet")
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}

This file now has the corrected clinic codes for each year. We want to merge it onto the GESIS mappings with a few manual adjustments:

#| format: file
s2_clinic_months_gesis_mapped_parquet <- {
  s2_clinic_months_corrected_parquet %>%
    read_parquet_duckdb() %>%
    mutate(
      # Treat missing conditions as false, preserving case_when() fall-through.
      map_year = if_else(
        coalesce(cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode <= 3, FALSE),
        "OLD GESIS 2015",
        if_else(
          coalesce(cAnnee == 2015 & fname == 1, FALSE),
          "OLD GESIS 2015",
          if_else(
            coalesce(cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode > 3, FALSE),
            "NEW GESIS 2015",
            # Cast to VARCHAR in DuckDB; as.character() is not translated.
            dd$cast_to_type(cAnnee, "")
          )
        )
      )
    ) %>% 
    left_join(
      s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df %>%
        
        # "gIAGmHMV9MS" -- in other years should map to "120143023" but NOT in 2013, when that's a different clinic 
        filter(!(fs_uid == "gIAGmHMV9MS" & cAnnee %in% c("2013", "2012"))) %>% 
        
        # similarly, this is not a good match, so drop it 
        filter(!(code_fs == "630242008" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015")) %>% 
        # the matching between GESIS code 110543027 in 2014 with UID qCHtCHkwqtQ causes trouble, lets unmatch here 
        mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == 110543027 & cAnnee == "2014", "", fs_uid)) %>% 
        transmute(
          map_year = cAnnee, 
          correct_cCodeStru = as.character(code_fs), 
          TYPE, fs_uid, 
          map_name = FS
        ), 
      by = c("correct_cCodeStru", "map_year")
    ) -> result
  
  output_path <- here::here("data", "intermediates", "unique_clinic_months_gesis_mapped.parquet")
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}
s2_gesis_code_deletions_raw_csv <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping\\.csv$"
)

s2_gesis_snips_verified_csv <- s2_pipeline_input_select_single_fn(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "GESIS_snips_public_multipleLongGESIS VERIFIED\\.csv$"
)
Tip Procedure: Correct GESIS Codes And Reconcile UIDs

The first transformation reproduces the reviewed code corrections, year-aware mapping join, UID fill rules, and clinic-name fallback from the legacy script. The mapping join retains its three documented exceptions: the UID that must not match in 2012–2013, the invalid old-2015 code, and the 2014 UID/code mismatch. Only the reduced six-column inventory is collected into R. For scale, the archived legacy inventory has 454,914 rows and occupies approximately 13 MB as an R object; the tall measurement tables remain outside R throughout ingestion.

Clinic names are already UTF-8 after import. The legacy stri_encode(from = "ISO-8859-1") step is therefore removed: decoding them a second time would turn Santé into SantÃ© before the existing ASCII name normalization.

s2_clinic_ids_corrected_df <- {
  clinic_month <- read_parquet_duckdb(
    s2_clinic_months_inventory_parquet, prudence = "stingy"
  ) |>
    arrange(.inventory_file, .inventory_row) |>
    select(all_of(s2_clinic_months_identity_columns_fn())) |>
    collect() |>
    mutate(across(!c(cAnnee, cPeriode, fname), as.character))

  gesis_correct <- readxl::read_excel(s2_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx) |>
    filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`), `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") |>
    setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) |>
    unique()

  clinic_month <- clinic_month |>
    left_join(
      gesis_correct |> select(cCodeStru = old_code, correct_cCodeStru = correct_code)
    ) |>
    mutate(correct_cCodeStru = coalesce(correct_cCodeStru, cCodeStru)) |>
    mutate(
      map_year = case_when(
        cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode <= 3 ~ "OLD GESIS 2015",
        cAnnee == 2015 & fname == 1 ~ "OLD GESIS 2015",
        cAnnee == 2015 & cPeriode > 3 ~ "NEW GESIS 2015",
        TRUE ~ as.character(cAnnee)
      )
    ) |>
    left_join(
      s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df |>
        filter(!(fs_uid == "gIAGmHMV9MS" & cAnnee %in% c("2013", "2012"))) |>
        filter(!(code_fs == "630242008" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015")) |>
        mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == 110543027 & cAnnee == "2014", "", fs_uid)) |>
        transmute(
          map_year = cAnnee,
          correct_cCodeStru = as.character(code_fs),
          TYPE,
          fs_uid,
          map_name = FS
        ),
      by = c("correct_cCodeStru", "map_year")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      group_uid = {
        values <- unique(na.omit(fs_uid))
        case_when(
          length(values) == 1L ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(values),
          length(values) == 2L & any(values == "") ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(setdiff(values, ""))
        )
      },
      .by = c(correct_cCodeStru, cNom)
    ) |>
    mutate(
      fs_uid = ifelse(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == "", group_uid, fs_uid)
    ) |>
    group_by(fs_uid, correct_cCodeStru, cNom) |>
    mutate(across(c(TYPE, map_name), list(uid = ~ {
      mode <- s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (dplyr::n_distinct(mode) == 1L) mode else NA
    }))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(TYPE = coalesce(TYPE, TYPE_uid), map_name = coalesce(map_name, map_name_uid)) |>
    select(-TYPE_uid, -map_name_uid, -group_uid) |>
    mutate(
      clean_name = ifelse(
        is.na(map_name),
        cNom |>
          stringi::stri_trans_general(id = "Latin-ASCII") |>
          str_trim() |>
          str_squish() |>
          stringr::str_remove("^CSB2|^CSB1|^CSB|CBS") |>
          tolower(),
        map_name
      ),
      clinic_ID = ifelse(
        is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == "",
        paste0(correct_cCodeStru, " - ", clean_name),
        fs_uid
      )
    )

  delete_codes <- read_csv(s2_gesis_code_deletions_raw_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(NOTE == "DELETE") |>
    pull(clinic_code) |>
    as.character()

  clinic_month |>
    mutate(
      clinic_ID = case_when(
        correct_cCodeStru == "610351004" & cAnnee == 2016 ~ NA_character_,
        correct_cCodeStru %in% delete_codes ~ NA_character_,
        TRUE ~ clinic_ID
      )
    )
}
Tip Procedure: Apply Reviewed Snips And Commune Matches

Verified GESIS snips and commune–clinic-name pairs can join records whose IDs differ. Four reviewed snips remain excluded because they were judged ambiguous. The 2014 exception for code 110543027 is retained.

s2_clinic_ids_reconciled_df <- {
  snips <- read_csv(s2_gesis_snips_verified_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(!is.na(GESIS_short)) |>
    mutate(GESIS_short = as.character(GESIS_short)) |>
    transmute(
      GESIS_snip = GESIS_short,
      verified_snip = `VERIFIED..1.CORRECT...0.INCORRECT.`
    )

  s2_clinic_ids_corrected_df |>
    mutate(
      GESIS_snip = paste0(str_sub(correct_cCodeStru, 1, 4), str_sub(correct_cCodeStru, 7, 9))
    ) |>
    left_join(
      snips |>
        filter(!GESIS_snip %in% c("1104006", "1104060", "5205039", "5202030")) |>
        filter(verified_snip == "1"),
      by = "GESIS_snip"
    ) |>
    group_by(GESIS_snip) |>
    mutate(
      clinic_ID = case_when(
        n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & any(fs_uid != "") & verified_snip == "1" ~
          s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(setdiff(fs_uid, ""), na.rm = TRUE)),
        n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & verified_snip == "1" ~
          s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE)),
        TRUE ~ clinic_ID
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      commune_name = paste0(cCodeNiv, " - ", gsub("^CSB1 |^CSB2 |^CSB ", "", clean_name))
    ) |>
    group_by(commune_name) |>
    mutate(
      clinic_ID = case_when(
        correct_cCodeStru == "110543027" & cAnnee == 2014 ~ clinic_ID,
        n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 & any(fs_uid != "") ~
          s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(setdiff(fs_uid, ""), na.rm = TRUE)),
        n_distinct(clinic_ID) > 1 ~ s2_clinic_ids_first_fn(s2_clinic_ids_mode_fn(clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE)),
        TRUE ~ clinic_ID
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}
Warning Check: Write And Inspect The Clinic ID Crosswalk

The final crosswalk keeps the legacy columns and ID_checked indicator. Rows without a clinic ID are retained in the intermediate artifact for review; the 31 expected removals are not silently dropped here.

s2_clinic_ids_df <- s2_clinic_ids_reconciled_df |>
  group_by(clinic_ID) |>
  mutate(ID_checked = any(grepl("CSB", TYPE))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    clinic_ID, cAnnee, cPeriode, cCodeNiv, cCodeStru,
    correct_cCodeStru, cNom, fname,
    type_map = TYPE, ID_checked
  )
#| format: file
s2_clinic_ids_rds <- {
  path <- here::here("data", "intermediates", "w2010_2019_clinicID.rds")
  dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(s2_clinic_ids_df, path)
  path
}
#| format: file
s2_clinic_ids_csv <- {
  path <- here::here("data", "intermediates", "w2010_2019_clinicID.csv")
  dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  write.csv(s2_clinic_ids_df, path, na = "", row.names = TRUE)
  path
}

The legacy workflow writes both RDS and CSV copies. The targets graph tracks them independently so each can be rebuilt and checked as a file artifact.

Run the encoding regression check from the repository root:

scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run tests/check-clinic-month-encoding.R

The fixture places French characters after the CSV sniffing sample and checks Windows-1252 decoding, quoted fields, missing values, deduplication, and original row order against read.csv(fileEncoding = "CP1252"). To also compare the complete January 2010 and January 2015 members against that independent reader:

scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run tests/check-clinic-month-encoding.R -- \
  data/inputs/01_gold_mine/gdn_datafreeze_may2025/madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning.zip
